title: The RIQ burn-rate alert never fired
scenario: On 2026-11-04 riq-api on prod-blue returned 503 for about 6% of requests for 38 minutes: a 60x burn of a 99.9% SLO. Nobody was paged; Support found it. You get the rule file, the Alertmanager config and silences, the old ServiceMonitor and the new PodMonitoring, the repo history, the rule evaluator log and a TSDB extract you can replay offline.
task: Replay the rules over the incident and find why the fast-burn alert stayed silent
Rule out the Alertmanager route change and the canary silence with evidence
Fix rules/riq-slo.rules.yaml for managed collection labels; decide per-cluster or aggregated
Add a guard so an SLO alert whose selector matches nothing cannot stay silent
Root cause, evidence and follow-ups in ANSWER.md
acceptance: Fast burn pages within 20 minutes of the outage start; healthy day and a 4-minute spike stay quiet
Slow burn (6h/30m at 6x) pages a burn rate of 12; burn rate 16 pages fast
An outage on one of two clusters pages within 40 minutes
A guard alert fires when the SLO series disappear; root cause and evidence in ANSWER.md
